narrative: The model estimated a 34% chance that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is a substantial risk, and under the school’s decision rule it places you in the group required to take remedial courses. The strongest factors in your profile actually worked in your favor: you have no past class failures, you want to continue to higher education, and your father completed secondary education. These are protective signals, which is why your estimated risk is not higher. The failure prediction comes instead from the accumulation of less dominant concerns, especially your very low weekly study time, your eight absences compared with the average of about four, and other lifestyle and health factors. Your family context may add pressure, but it is not among the strongest reasons. To improve, focus on consistent weekly study, attend school more regularly, and seek support early from your teachers or family. Treat the remedial courses as a structured way to build those habits and reduce the risk that this prediction becomes a reality.
